quotes.text: Windows 365 link is a physical device built for one job, connecting you to a Windows 365 cloud PC. That definition matters because the device and the cloud PC are not the same thing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates the access device from the Cloud PC in one clear definition.

quotes.text: Intune manages the small link device at the desk while Windows 365 and Intune manage the actual cloud PC where the user works. One is the access point, the other is the working desktop.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the two management layers behind the device.

quotes.text: For people who travel often, work in areas with unreliable internet or need to keep working during an outage, a regular laptop remains the better tool.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States plainly when the device is the wrong choice.

quotes.text: Buy Windows 365 link for a clear work pattern. Do not buy it just because it is the newest small box from Microsoft.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Windows 365 link is a focused access device, not a general PC. When the work pattern fits, that limitation is exactly why it works.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode's thesis that the device's limits are its strength.

takeaways: Windows 365 Link is a purpose-built access device: the Windows desktop, apps and files run in a Windows 365 Cloud PC, while the box on the desk only connects the user to it.
Entra ID handles identity, Intune manages the device and the Cloud PC, and Windows 365 provides the workspace, with TPM, secure boot, BitLocker and no local admin keeping the device locked down.
The device fits shared desks, shift work and contact centers with reliable networks, but not offline, mobile or developer roles, and it does not work with Azure Virtual Desktop.
hook: Windows 365 Link looks like a small PC but works very differently, and many teams misjudge where it fits. This episode helps IT administrators and decision-makers understand the device, Cloud PCs, Entra ID and Intune, and decide whether shared-desk and frontline scenarios justify a rollout.
